drone-regulatory-frameworks.title: Permissions have several layers
drone-regulatory-frameworks.description: Framework overview through 19 October 2026. The UK follows its own national regime.
rows: Aircraft category and activity determine the route. Operator certification, applicable airworthiness requirements and insurance are separate layers. CCAR-92 governs civil operating safety. [C02][C03][C04]
Part 135 supports relevant package-delivery operations, with applicable aircraft and BVLOS permissions. The examined Part 108 material is a proposal, not an effective rule. [G01][G02][G03]

BVLOS commonly falls in the specific category, usually requiring national-authority authorization. Standard-scenario and relevant LUC privileges provide exceptions; higher-risk operations may be certified. [G06]
Controlled airspace requires approval. Fixed-airspace routine operations can seek long-term applications; the actual aircraft, activity and operating conditions still matter. [C02]
UTM shares flight intent and real-time constraints. Operators remain responsible for safe operations; this is not positive FAA air traffic control. Separate airspace permissions apply. [G01]
Within designated U-space airspace, mandatory services include network identification, geo-awareness, flight authorization and traffic information. [G04][G05]
An operator certificate does not permit every route or airspace. Airworthiness exemptions remain relevant; airspace below 120 metres is not universally unrestricted. [C02][C03]
Air-carrier certification does not replace aircraft authorization, environmental review or local requirements. A proposed future framework is not proof of current nationwide access. [G01][G02][G03]
A U-space service-provider certificate does not replace operator authorization. EU rules becoming applicable does not mean U-space services are deployed everywhere. [G04][G05][G06]
Implementation remains location- and operation-specific. Permissions must match the aircraft category, activity and approved operating conditions. [C02][C03][C04]
Operators deploy under their applicable certifications and permissions. Approval lists do not measure active sites, completed deliveries or commercial profitability. [G01]
U-space rules apply from 26 January 2023. EASA issued its first USSP certificate to ANRA in May 2025; deployment still depends on designated airspace and services. [G04][G05]
drone-regulatory-frameworks.note:
Framework descriptions are not route-specific permission, an airspace-capacity guarantee or a measure of market size.
Sources: China [C02] [C03] [C04]; United States [G01] [G02] [G03]; EU / EASA [G04] [G05] [G06]. Full links accompany the data.
